definitions: The initial negative deflection of the QRS complex on an electrocardiogram, representing ventricular septal depolarization.
A downward deflection on an electrocardiogram (ECG) that occurs after the P wave and before the R wave, indicating the electrical activity of the ventricles.
examples: The presence of a pathological Q wave can indicate a previous myocardial infarction.
A normal Q wave is usually small and narrow.
The cardiologist analyzed the Q wave morphology.
